correctness.rationale: For all integers \(q\ge1\), global domination is exactly four-part transversal support. In any partition each class support is proper and has a covering partner. Sorting the indices that occur as singleton supports into \(t=0,1,2,3,4\) gives bounds \(2q\), \(\max(2q,3q-3)\), \(\max(2q,3q-3)\), \(3q-3\), and \(4q-8\), respectively. The \(t=1\) incidence estimate uses one mandatory triple and one extra mixed support when present; the \(t=2\) estimate uses mandatory complementary triples and a required partner for every pair supported on the other two parts. Explicit constructions attain all three relevant expressions, and \(q=1\) is checked separately. Direct complete original-graph enumeration checks 15, 4140, and 4213597 partitions for \(q=1,2,3\), with independent support integer-program checks for \(1\le q\le25\). Computation corroborates but does not prove the infinite statement.

originality.rationale: The arXiv:2509.15386v4 source proves the global coalition lower construction and exact complete-tripartite case, then states its multipartite sharpness conjecture as Conjecture 54. The balanced four-part upper bound is not implied by these statements. Multiple literature and research-record searches using original and complementary graph formulations found no equivalent result. This is a best-knowledge priority judgment, not an independence guarantee.
residual_risks: Searches cannot exclude a differently phrased earlier exact formula, especially under the classical coalition parameter of the complement.
Mathematical correctness and priority have not been assessed by an independent researcher.

value.rationale: Determines a natural infinite first-open case (four balanced parts) of Conjecture 54 and proves a sharp upper bound missing from the published lower-bound construction. The exact value has three regimes and demonstrates a reusable support-incidence obstruction based on compulsory partner triples. This is neither a renamed previous lower bound nor a finite numerical slice.
